content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make fried parsley, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Wash the parsley bunches thoroughly (5 minutes)
Step 2. Set out a wire cooling rack (1 minute)
Step 3. Check the parsley for any wilted yellow leaves (3 minutes)
Step 4. Garnish the main dish with the fried parsley (2 minutes)
Step 5. Pat the parsley dry with paper towels (10 minutes)
Step 6. Clean the stove top (10 minutes)
Step 7. Dispose of the used frying oil (15 minutes)
Step 8. Season the fried parsley with fine sea salt (30 seconds)
Step 9. Remove the parsley from the oil with a slotted spoon (1 minute)
Step 10. Locate the kitchen thermometer (2 minutes)
Step 11. Pour vegetable oil into a heavy-bottomed pot (1 minute)
Step 12. Adjust the burner flame to maintain temperature (20 minutes)
Step 13. Trim the long stems off the parsley (4 minutes)
Step 14. Separate the parsley into small, uniform sprigs (8 minutes)
Step 15. Calibrate the kitchen thermometer in ice water (5 minutes)
Step 16. Spin the parsley in a salad spinner to remove deep moisture (3 minutes)
Step 17. Organize the sprigs on a prep tray (5 minutes)
Step 18. Compost the parsley roots (1 minute)
Step 19. Buy fresh flat-leaf parsley from the market (1 hour)
Step 20. Let the parsley air dry on a clean cloth (30 minutes)
Step 21. Heat the oil to 350 degrees Fahrenheit (12 minutes)
Step 22. Place a paper-towel-lined plate near the stove (2 minutes)
Step 23. Turn on the kitchen ventilation fan (10 seconds)
Step 24. Double-check the sprigs for any remaining water droplets (2 minutes)
Step 25. Ensure the parsley is bone-dry to prevent splattering (15 minutes)
Step 26. Prepare a bowl for the finished product (1 minute)
Step 27. Clip the thermometer to the side of the pot (30 seconds)
Step 28. Test a single sprig in the oil (30 seconds)
Step 29. Lay out the dry parsley for final inspection (2 minutes)
Step 30. Clear a workspace on the counter (5 minutes)
Step 31. Arrange the frying equipment for easy reach (4 minutes)
Step 32. Transfer parsley sprigs to a dry bowl for frying (1 minute)
Step 33. Set out a timer (30 seconds)
Step 34. Carefully drop the parsley into the hot oil (10 seconds)
Step 35. Fry the parsley until translucent and crisp (45 seconds)
Step 36. Drain the parsley briefly over the pot (20 seconds)
Step 37. Check the oil level in the pot (30 seconds)
Step 38. Allow the parsley to cool slightly (3 minutes)
Step 39. Wipe down the kitchen counters (10 minutes)
Step 40. Transfer the fried parsley to the lined plate (30 seconds)
